study.title: Light and Hiding
study.focus: Why do people run from the light, and what does it look like to come to it?
study.take: This take follows the heart. The passages chosen here trace why people choose the dark (3:19), what they fear in the light (3:20), and what coming to it looks like (3:21).
study.question: What is one thing you tend to keep in the dark, and what would it mean to bring it to the light?
study.closing: In these passages, coming to the light does not start with being clean. It starts with no longer hiding.

scripture.19: This is the judgment, that the light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light, for their works were evil.
scripture.20: For everyone who does evil hates the light and doesn’t come to the light, lest his works would be exposed.
scripture.21: But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his works may be revealed, that they have been done in God.”

summaries.CAL3.19.02: John Calvin says no one should blame Christ for his condemnation. Unbelief shows a bad conscience: people's own wickedness keeps them from coming to Christ.
summaries.MHC3.19.04: Matthew Henry says people love darkness because their deeds are evil. They are in love with their sickness and slavery, and hate the light because it robs them of their good opinion of themselves.
summaries.GIL3.20.02: John Gill says the one who does evil avoids the light so his deeds are not exposed, shamed and blamed, and so that he is not told to give them up.
summaries.MHC3.20.06: Matthew Henry says Christ is hated because sin is loved; staying away from the light shows a hidden hatred of saving knowledge.
summaries.JFB3.21.01: Jamieson, Fausset and Brown say the one who does truth wants only what can bear the light, so he comes to it and is shown to be God's work.
summaries.AUG3.19-21.2.05: Augustine says doing the truth begins when we stop flattering ourselves and calling ourselves righteous. Even our displeasure at our sin comes from God shining his truth into us.
